text:
sam: quick follow-up from the RFC sync — we need to reconcile edge affinity heuristics with the new pipelining change. what are the non-negotiables?
priya: non-negotiable = preserve 99th latency SLO for paid tiers. everything else can be softened. :lock: :chart_with_downwards_trend:
marcus: agree. also want to avoid cross-region cold-starts for long-seq jobs, those blow up tail latency.
li: can we special-case >1024 token requests to stick to local leased capacity? otherwise allow cross-region fallbacks for small requests.
daniela: that seems reasonable but watch cost — keeping large seqs local increases reserved capacity needs.
sam: thinking of hybrid rule: prefer local affinity score + penalty for lease exhaustion, but allow preemptible spill to cheaper region if latency delta < 100ms for embeddings and <50ms for chat.
paul: can you sketch the scoring formula? short snippet would help ops/infra.
sam: sure — rough draft: ```score = base_score - latency_ms*0.01 - cost_multiplier*10 - lease_penalty; if seq_len > 1024: score += seq_affinity_bonus;```
marcus: inline comment: cost_multiplier is 0.5 for on-demand, 0.2 for preemptible, 1.0 for dedicated. seems fine.
priya: also add tenant_tier_multiplier (free=0.8, paid=1.2) so we don't route paid traffic to cheapest fallback unless necessary.
li: + add a jitter factor to avoid thundering in failover e.g., small rand([-5,5]) to score.
daniela: ops concern — when leases expire we should instantaneously reduce score, not wait for next evaluation window. otherwise we get bursts.
op s-bot: lease-watchdog: lease 0x7f expired for region-us-east-1 at 1998765460
paul: maybe implement lease decay: lease_penalty = max_penalty * exp(-time_since_expiry / tau) so penalty fades. set tau to 30s.
sam: good idea. that prevents immediate flip-flopping.
marcus: another tradeoff: batching/pipelining benefit means prefer putting small requests with similar model onto same machine to hit kernel warm paths. that is orthogonal to region affinity but interacts with cost.
priya: can we add a constraint that pipelines only when estimated batch latency < SLO_margin? so we don't batch if it risks SLO.
li: suggest adding a precheck: estimate_batch_time = current_kernel_latency * (1 + queued_tokens/typical_batch); if estimate_batch_time > slo_margin -> disable pipeline for that tenant.
daniela: ops/observability ask: expose per-tenant routing decisions and justification tag (e.g., "seq_affinity_bonus", "cost_fallback") in Console for 30d.
sam: agreed — add tags. also we need a compact rollout plan: 1) sim mode (no routing changes, log decisions) 2) canary (5% traffic) 3) rollout by tenant tier 4) full.
priya: can we include a kill-switch that forces strict-local for paid tiers? sales asked for that.
paul: yes, add runtime flag `route.strict_local_paid=true`.
li: one more: tie-breaking when scores equal — prefer lower cost unless forced by SLA. add stable ordering by region id to avoid oscillation.
sam: next steps: implement scoring hook + telemetry, run sim for 48h, surface top 10 divergent cases. volunteers?
daniela: ops can run sim and collection.
marcus: i'll own the scoring hook and unit tests.
priya: i'll write the canary rollout doc and add kill-switch.
paul: infra will add lease decay metric and the precheck estimator.
sam: awesome. I'll file a follow-up RFC PR with the scoring snippet and rollout checklist. thanks all :tada:
